correctness.rationale: For each n≥0 the original Esakia X_n has levels L_i of m+1=2^n+1 points and unique minimum. Order automorphisms preserve each L_i because iteratively deleting maximal levels recovers all levels. In adjacent-level incidence x_{i+1}^l≤x_i^u iff u≠l+1, so x_i^0 is the unique upper vertex adjacent from all lower-level points, and s_i maps each lower label l<m intrinsically to its uniquely missing upper label l+1. Iterating k such intrinsic maps from x_{i+k}^0 recovers every x_i^k. All points therefore fixed, including n=0. Esakia dual equivalence transfers trivial group to H_n=X_n*. Independently enumerated all compatible adjacent-level permutations of widths 2 through 5 (counts 1,2,6,24) and verified characteristic endpoint/missing-upper relations; the all-n conclusion rests on the exact order argument.

originality.rationale: The source Hyttinen–Martins–Moraschini–Quadrellaro introduces the very spaces X_n and proves strict n-finiteness, but its inspected original paper supplies no automorphism-rigidity result. Previous monogenic size spectra of the dual algebras do not logically imply rigidity. A short argument may be classical at n=0 or folklore for all n; the uniform intrinsic labeling result is distinct.
residual_risks: Uniform proof short; corresponding rigidity may be known informally, and the n=0 Rieger–Nishimura automorphism case may be classical.
The finite compatible-pair enumeration is not itself an infinite group classification; analytic level induction provides that.
The conclusion concerns precisely these X_n and H_n, not arbitrary strictly n-finite Heyting algebras.
